Date : 15/07/2024  ORAL ORDER 1.

The present First Appeal, under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, is preferred by the appellants - original claimants - legal heirs of the deceased - Ushaben, being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the judgment and award dated 14.02.2019 passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal (Aux.), Arvalli at Modasa in Motor Accident Claim Petition No.49 of 2016, by which the Tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.15,02,461/- with 9% per annum interest to the claimant/s, holding opponents liable, jointly and severally.

2.1 On 16.12.2015 at about 05:00 p.m. in the evening on the road of Modasa to Shamlaji and in the sim of village Ganeshpur, at that time, the wife of the claimant no.1 and mother of the claimant no.2 namely - Ushaben, was standing on the right Ramanlal Mafatlal Prajapati vs The New India Assurance Company Limited on 15 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89585759/

sentences.text: At that time, opponent no.1 driven his truck bearing Regd. No.GJ-09-Z- 1412 in excessive speed, in rash and negligent manner engendering human life and dashed his truck behind the deceased on account of which, accident took place and deceased sustained fatal injuries and she was died during treatment on 10/01/2016.

It is further case of the claimants that accident took place due the negligence of opponent no.1.
2.2

Therefore, the legal heirs of the deceased have filed claim petition seeking compensation of Rs.50 lakhs with cost and interest for unnatural and untimely death against the present respondents before the Tribunal.
2.2 Notices were served to the opponents.
Opponents No.1 and 2 - driver and owner have chosen not to appear and contest the claim petition before the Tribunal.
Opponent No.3 - Insurance Company has appeared and has filed its written statement / objections at Exh.17 by disputing all the averments made by the claimant/s in the claim petition.
2.3 The Tribunal has framed the issues at Exh.18.
The oral as well as documentary evidence were led by the rival parties before the Tribunal.
After considering the documentary as well as oral evidence and submissions made at the bar, the Tribunal has partly allowed the claim petition by awarding compensation as noted above.
2.4 Being aggrieved and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal,

the present appeal is preferred by NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/181/2022 ORDER DATED:
15/07/2024 undefined the claimant/s for enhancement.
3. Learned advocate the appellants - claimants has submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error in not properly calculating the amount of compensation.

It is submitted that amount of award is on lower side as the Tribunal has not properly considered the various aspects; like income of the deceased, negligence, prospective income, loss of estate, consortium, and funeral expenses, liability and family circumstances, etc.

It is submitted that the deceased was doing agriculture work and drudgery work and thereby, earning Rs.6,000/- per month, hence, the Tribunal has erroneously considered Rs.4,500/- p.m. income of the deceased.

It is further submitted that looking to the age of the deceased i.e. 51 years, and keeping in view the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited versus Pranay Shethi reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680,
10% income should be added towards prospective income of the deceased, which the Tribunal has committed error in considering to the extent 25%.

sentences.text: Further, it is submitted that the Tribunal has rightly deducted 1/3 amount towards personal expenses.

He has fairly submitted that the Tribunal has not committed error by applying the multiplier, which should be 11 keeping in view the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the Sarla Verma versus Delhi Transport Corporation reported in (2009) 6 SCC 121.

Therefore,
the Tribunal has committed error by not properly awarding compensation under the head of loss of consortium.

It is submitted that in view of various above-mentioned decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, Rs.25,000/- instead of Rs.15,000/- towards transportation, Rs.1 lakh instead of 15,000/-
towards pain, shock and suffering and Rs.12,00,000/- instead of Rs.8,67,461/- towards annual medical expenditure is required to be awarded.

It is submitted that under other heads except above,
the Tribunal has rightly considered the amount of compensation.
It is submitted that the compensation is required to be enhanced by modifying the award impugned accordingly and this appeal may be allowed.
4. Per contra, learned advocate for contesting respondents has submitted that the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal is just and proper.
The Tribunal has rightly considered the income of the deceased.
It is submitted that the Tribunal has committed an error by adding prospective income on higher side.
It is also submitted that under the head of loss of estate and funeral expenses, the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation.
It is also submitted that under the head of loss of consortium, the Tribunal has considered proper compensation.

However, from the submissions made by learned advocate for the appellants that the Tribunal has committed certain errors, on this aspect, learned advocates for the respondent/s has submitted that if this Court feels that there is some NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/181/2022 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined error in calculation of the amount in view of settled position of law, in awarding compensation by the Tribunal, then the Court may pass appropriate order by considering the submissions made by learned advocate for the appellant/s, in the interest of justice.
It is submitted that this appeal may be dismissed and no interference be made by this Court.

sentences.text: It is noteworthy to mention that the provisions of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 which gives paramount importance to the concept of 'just and fair' compensation.
It is a beneficial legislation which has been framed with the object of providing relief to the victims or their families.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act deals with the concept of 'just compensation' which ought to be determined on the foundation of fairness, reasonableness and equitability.

Although such determination can never be arithmetically exact or perfect, an endeavor should be made by the Court to award just and fair compensation irrespective of the amount claimed by the claimants.
6.1 I have considered the submissions made by the rival parties.
I have perused the record and proceedings of the Tribunal.
I have gone through the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal.

It is noted that the claimant has by and large claimed enhancement towards income of the deceased, negligence, prospective income, loss of estate, consortium, and funeral expenses, liability and family circumstances, etc.
It transpires that the Tribunal has taken into consideration the monthly income of the claimant Rs.1,200/-.

As the deceased was doing agriculture work and drudgery work and thereby, earning Rs.6,000/- per month as per submission, hence, the Tribunal has erroneously considered Rs.4,500/- p.m. NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/181/2022 ORDER DATED: 15/07/2024 undefined income of the deceased as per submission, the monthly income of injured should be considered Rs.6,000/-, instead of Rs.4,500/- as awarded by the Tribunal.

Furthermore, looking to the age of the deceased at the time of accident, i.e. 51 years and considering the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Shethi (supra), 10% rise should be added as prospective income.
Therefore, it would come to Rs.6,600/- per month income of the deceased.

Further, considering the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra) and Pranay Shethi (supra), 1/3 would be the deduction towards personal expense, which is rightly considered by the Tribunal.

Therefore, it would come to Rs.4,400/- per month multiplied by 12 months (annual income) and further multiplied by 11 multiplier keeping in view the decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra), it would come to Rs.5,80,800/- as future loss of income, which should be awarded by the Tribunal.

6.2 Further, under the head of loss of consortium, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.80,000/- only,
which should be on higher side.
It is not in dispute that there are two dependents in the family.

In view of the decisions of Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of : (i) Magma General Insurance Company Limited versus Nanu Ram and others reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130 (ii) New India Assurance Co.
Ltd. v. Somwati and others, reported in 2020 (9) SCC 644 and (iii) United India Insurance Co. Ltd.,
versus Satinder Kaur @ Satwinder Kaur reported in (2021) 11 SCC 780, under the head of loss of consortium, Rs.48,400/- each would be proper to award, therefore, Rs.48,400/- x 2 dependents =
Rs.96,800/- would be the compensation under the head of loss of consortium.

Furthermore, under other heads except the above, the amount awarded by the Tribunal is not disputed by learned advocate for the appellant/s, otherwise also, the Tribunal has rightly considered the amount under those heads.
